dataset.name: Meteorological Conditions and Atmospheric Components Concentration in Urban Sites in Knoxville, USA. 2024
description: This dataset, which contains five csv files, reports several meteorological conditions such as temperature, wind speed, solar radiation, and net radiation measured in Cumberland Estates Park (CEP) and Socially Equal Energy Efficient Development (SEEED) sites in Knoxville, Tennessee, USA. Also, hourly concentration of particulate matter (PM) with different aerodynamic diameter and inorganic gases such as ozone and nitrogen dioxide measured in the two are included in this dataset. The concentrations of PM and inorganic gases were monitored using the MODULAIR, a low-cost sensor equipped with a solar power module. The measurement of the concentration of biogenic and anthropogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of the two sites was determined using a High-Resolution Proton Transfer Reaction Time of Flight Mass Spectrometer (PTR-ToF-MS). The VOCs were collected using miniature canister (400 mL) equipped with female RAVEqc valve to 1/4” male compression fitting and an integrated passive air sampling kit. This work is a part of a larger study which investigates the impact of soil moisture and plant evapotranspiration on ambient temperature and relative humidity in several city parks in Knoxville, Tennessee.

spatialCoverage.description: Cumberland Estates Park (CEP) located in Knoxville, Tennessee. This site is 26 acres of fenced park which consists of forest, unpaved trails, picnic tables, and playground. Instruments at CEP were collocated at the parking lot next to the forested area. Elevation: 339 meters

Socially Equal Energy Efficient Development (SEEED) site is non-governmental organization in proximity to downtown Knoxville (~1.0 mile) that experiences busy transportation activity. The instrument in the SEEED site was deployed near an open forest with fruit trees, vegetables, and herbs that are freely available to the public. Elevation: 323 meters

measurementTechnique: MODULAIR (QuantAQ, Inc. Massachusetts, USA), a low cost and portable sensor, was used to continuously measure the real-time concentration of particulate matter with different diameter (0.35 to 40 µm, 24 bins). MODULAIR also monitor inorganic gases, which include carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxide (NO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and ozone (O3). The MODULAIR is integrated with solar power module. Information regarding the atmospheric moisture (relative humidity) was also monitored by the MODULAIR. METER ATMOS 41 All-in-One Weather Station (Pullman, Washington, USA) was deployed in the site to record the air temperature, wind speed and direction, and solar radiation. Apogee (Logan, Utah, USA) net radiometer (Model SN-500-SS) was also included in the weather station to observe incident and emitted radiations.

Volatile organic compounds were collected using a 400 cc electropolished stainless steel with quick-connect stem fitting equipped with female RAVEqc valve to 1/4” male compression fitting and an integrated passive air sampling kit with 0.041 mm orifice size. The configuration of the miniature sample provided 4-8 ml per min vacuum flow, thus collecting ambient air for 1 hour sampling. Ambient air was sampled twice a week with two replicates per site. The contents of the canisters were measured using the High-Resolution Proton Transfer Reaction Time of Flight Mass Spectrometer (PTR-ToF-MS) 6000X2 (IONICON, Innsbruck, Austria). The PTR-ToF-MS ionize the gases through non-dissociative proton transfer inside the reaction chamber of the instrument. Several gases can be detected by the PTR-ToF-MS as long as the target compound has a proton affinity higher than water (691 kJ/mol). This discounts major gases such as CO2, NO, NO2, and O3 which can saturate the detector, thus focusing on the important organic compounds.
